title: Ball moved by an animal
question: A dog runs onto the fairway and knocks your ball out of its spot. According to the rules, what should you do?

choices.text: Play the ball from its new spot
Add a penalty and replace the ball

explanation: If an outside influence, such as an animal, moves your ball at rest, you must replace it without penalty.

juniorVersion.title: Dog moves your ball
juniorVersion.question: You are playing golf and a dog runs onto the grass, bumping your ball out of its place. What should you do?

choices.text: Hit your ball from where it stopped
Put your ball back where it was, no penalty
Add a penalty and put your ball back

juniorVersion.explanation: If an animal like a dog moves your ball, you must put the ball back where it was. You do not get a penalty.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: When you have to add extra shots to your score because you broke a rule.
The short grass between the start and the green.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Remind juniors that animals and people are called 'outside influences' in golf. Only replace the ball when an outside influence moves it.
likelyMisconceptions: Some juniors may think you always play the ball from wherever it ends up, but that's not true if an animal moves it.
Some may think you get a penalty, but you don't if an animal moves your ball.
